# Navigation and page structure (NV)

This is the short form. Before writing code in this area, read the full rules with reasons, bad/good examples and checks: `.ui-polish/rules/19-navigation.md`.

- **NV-01 The current location is always marked** (error). The navigation item for the current page carries `aria-current="page"` and a visible state that is not colour alone (weight, an indicator bar, a filled background), with at least 3:1 contrast. Section parents of the current page are marked too. Tabs use `aria-selected`. The page `<title>` and the `<h1>` name the same place.
- **NV-02 Landmarks and a skip link** (warning). Every page has one `<header>`, one `<main>` holding the page's content, a `<nav>` with an `aria-label` for each navigation block ("Primary", "Breadcrumbs", "Account"), and a `<footer>` if there is one. The first focusable element is a "Skip to content" link that becomes visible on focus and jumps to `<main>`.
- **NV-03 One page-header pattern** (warning). Every page starts the same way: breadcrumbs when the page is deeper than two levels (NV-04), then the `<h1>`, an optional one-line description, and the page's actions on the inline end, primary action last and filled, secondary actions outlined, the rest in a "More" menu. Tabs that switch views of the same object sit directly under the header. The header keeps the same spacing and position on every page.
- **NV-04 Breadcrumbs for depth** (info). Pages three or more levels deep show breadcrumbs: `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumbs">` around an `<ol>`, each ancestor a link, the current page last and marked `aria-current="page"`. Separators are decorative (CSS, hidden from screen readers). On narrow screens collapse the middle into a "…" menu and keep the first and last two items; never truncate the current page's name.
- **NV-05 Links go places, buttons do things** (error). Anything that changes the URL is an `<a href>` (it can be opened in a new tab, copied and bookmarked). Anything that acts on the page is a `<button type="button">`. Never `href="#"`, `href="javascript:…"`, or an `<a>` without `href` used as a button, and never a button that only navigates.
- **NV-06 View state lives in the URL** (warning). The selected tab, filters, search query, sort and page are reflected in the URL (path or query string), so reload, back, forward and sharing a link all return to the same view. Moving between pages keeps the user's scroll position on back. Dialogs that represent a place (a record's detail) can have their own URL; confirmations do not.
- **NV-07 The menu is short and grouped** (warning). Primary navigation has at most about seven items, ordered by use, with group labels for more; settings, help and the account menu sit apart from the work areas. Each item has an icon and a text label (IC-04); a collapsed sidebar keeps the icons with tooltips and remembers its state. Navigation labels are nouns for places ("Invoices"), not verbs.
